judged_before.why: The first judging held c08 without the game's own verdict from before the change and read c02 three ways (review R1 of the comparison's lane): judged again with the list of what passed before the change, and with c02 saying what the brief left open.

items.evidence: examples/win_seed1.json, seed 1: wave becomes 6 at tick 5415 (after wave 5 cleared, score 450). With the guard idle from 5400, runners spawn at ticks 5415, 5505, 5595... (90 ticks = 1.5 s apart), kind runner, health 1, x drops 0.05/tick = 3 units/s. Score went 450 -> 675 = 15 runners x 15 before 'won'.

'Wave n of 6' seen in en ('Wave 6 of 6'), es ('Oleada 6 de 6'), fr ('Vague 6 sur 6'); full clear on Normal = won, 675; runner kills add 15. But the run is not won only when the last runner is destroyed: win script cut to idle at tick 6550 -> 3 runners reach the gate (gate 5 -> 2), screen 'won' with score 630 at tick 7100, last runner never destroyed.

Settings Right on Language: en -> es -> fr -> en (Left from en gives fr). With language fr, texts on title, settings, play, paused, won, lost are all French ('Défendez la porte', 'Réglages', 'Vague 1 sur 6', 'En pause', 'Gagné !', 'Perdu !', 'Entrée : titre'...); frames show the same in French. ('Score', 'Volume', 'Normal' are also French words.)

Settings texts: Settings, Volume, Language, Difficulty: Normal, Back (menu index 2 = Difficulty, 3 = Back). Right: normal->hard->easy->normal, Left: normal->easy. Default normal. Shown as 'Dificultad: Fácil/Normal/Difícil' and 'Difficulté : Facile/Normal/Difficile'; frame f_settings_fr shows it marked.

First walker health at spawn: easy 1, normal 2, hard 3 (hard walker took 3 hits to die). Runners: normal 1 and easy 1 seen; on Hard my closed-loop bot reached wave 6 and the first runner had health 2 (then won 675).

One run set volume 7, fr, easy via the menu; file kept {volume 7, language fr, difficulty easy}; next run with the same file started at 7/fr/easy and spawned walkers with health 1. Old-format file {volume 7, language es} loads as 7/es/normal; a missing file gives 5/en/normal.
State JSON has "difficulty" and each walker has "kind" (walker/runner). hold.py frame wrote PNGs whose header reads 800 x 480 for title, settings, play, paused, won, lost.

Rechecked m01-m19 on the changed game (see notes): title/start/settings, volume clamp 0..10, Spanish, persistence, guard 6 u/s clamp 0..12, bolt every 24 ticks at 14 u/s gone past 20, wave 1 = 5 walkers 90 ticks apart at 1.5 u/s in lanes 2..10, 2 hits = +10, gate drop and lost, wave 2 180 ticks after wave 1 cleared with 7 walkers, won 675 then Enter -> title, pause freezes/resume/title, same seed identical, other seeds other lanes, frames match state.

CHANGES.md lists each change with files (game.rs, lib.rs, draw.rs, strings/fr.json, strings.rs, hold.py, example script), what was checked and how (cargo tests, hold.py runs, frames), and what was found wrong before.

defects: A run is won when wave 6 ends with runners having reached the gate (score below 675), not only when the last runner is destroyed; README/CHANGES call this a deliberate choice.
Acute accents (É) are drawn as a single dot above the letter in the frame, which reads like Ė rather than É.
hold.py writes settings.json into work/ by default (next to hold.py) unless --settings is given.

items.evidence: Seed 1 Normal, own bot script via hold.py run: wave 6 begins tick 5414 (180 ticks after wave 5 cleared at score 450); a new runner at x=20 appears at 5415+90k for k=0..14 and none at k=15 (15 runners), each kind runner, health 1; an unshot runner goes 20 -> 18.5 -> 17 -> 15.5 in 30-tick steps (3 units/s).

HUD 'Wave n of 6' / 'Oleada n de 6' / 'Vague n sur 6' (seen waves 1, 2, 5, 6). After wave 5 cleared (score 450) the screen stays play and wave 6 follows. Full clear: won, 675 on Easy, Normal and Hard. Bot stopped at the last spawn: the last runner went through the gate (5 -> 4) and the screen turned won the same tick, score 660.

Right on Language: en -> es -> fr -> en; Left from en gives fr. French texts on title, settings (Facile/Normal/Difficile), play, paused, won and lost are all French ('Défendez la porte', 'Réglages', 'Vague 6 sur 6', 'Santé de la porte', 'En pause', 'Reprendre', 'Gagné !', 'Perdu !', 'Entrée : titre'). I saw no English, Spanish or missing keys, and the frames show the French with accents.

Settings texts: Volume, Language, Difficulty, Back (Difficulty at menu_index 2). Fresh settings give 'Difficulty: Normal'. Right gives Hard, Left gives Easy (wrapping). Shown as 'Dificultad: Fácil/Difícil' and 'Difficulté : Facile/Difficile'. The fr_settings frame shows the row highlighted.

Wave 1's first walker has health 1/2/3 on easy/normal/hard. Wave 6's first runner, reached by my bot through the engine on each difficulty, has health 1 (easy), 1 (normal) and 2 (hard). The Hard bot then won 675.

Run 1 set volume 7, fr and easy, and the settings file kept them. Run 2 started with volume 7, fr and easy, and its walkers had 1 health. An old-format file {volume:7,language:es} loads as 7/es/normal. A missing file gives 5/en/normal.

Every run state has 'difficulty' (easy/normal/hard), and every walker has 'kind' (walker/runner). Every PNG written by hold.py frame (title, settings, play, paused, won, lost) has an 800x480 PNG header.
Re-ran all m01-m19 through the engine and frames (see below), reading them with 'of 6' and 675; all still pass.

CHANGES.md lists each of the three changes with the files touched (game.rs, draw.rs, lib.rs, strings/*.json, strings.rs, hold.py, example script, README). It says what was checked and how (cargo tests, engine runs, frames), names what was not checked, and lists what it found wrong before.

defects: Frame: with the guard at y=12 (top edge), the guard and its bolts are drawn mostly under the HUD bar and are hard to see. This looks inherited from before the change.
Frame font: the acute accent (É) is drawn as a single dot above the letter, so it reads like Ė (cosmetic).
hold.py's default --settings writes settings.json inside the game folder next to hold.py (documented, but a run without --settings leaves a file in work/).

where.how: weighted_by_kind is exact (the run's own token counts times the weights); a step's kind is a reading of its command's text, and answered_tokens / written_tokens are characters / 4
